## Mapping reads to RAD loci

```{bash}
FASTQDIR=../2023-05-17b/crepi_edits
if [ ! -e radloci.fa.fai ]; then
   if [ ! -e radloci.fa ]; then
      cp ../2024-10-03/consensus.fa ./radloci.fa
   fi
   samtools faidx radloci.fa
fi
if [ ! -e radloci.fa.bwt.2bit.64 ]; then
   bwa-mem2 index radloci.fa &> /dev/null
fi
if [ ! -e samples.txt ]; then
   gawk '(NR > 1){
      gsub(/"/,"",$3)
      print substr($3,1,7)
   }' ../../data/IDs/Crepido_fish_IDs_all_data_2021Dec.txt | \
   sort | uniq > samples.txt
fi

if [ ! -d BAM ]; then mkdir BAM; fi
for SAMPLE in $(cat samples.txt); do
   if [ ! -e BAM/${SAMPLE}.bam ]; then
      if [ ! -e BAM/${SAMPLE}.sam ]; then
         bwa-mem2 mem -t 12 radloci.fa \
            $FASTQDIR/${SAMPLE}.trimmed_R1_.fastq.gz \
            $FASTQDIR/${SAMPLE}.trimmed_R2_.fastq.gz \
            -R "@RG\tID:${SAMPLE}\tSM:${SAMPLE}" 1> BAM/${SAMPLE}.sam 2>> bwamem2.log
      fi
      # Exclude (-F) unmapped reads (4) and secondary alignments (256). Include only proper pairs.
      samtools view -F 260 -f 2 -u BAM/${SAMPLE}.sam | \
      samtools sort > BAM/${SAMPLE}.bam
      samtools index BAM/${SAMPLE}.bam
      if [ -e BAM/${SAMPLE}.sam ]; then rm BAM/${SAMPLE}.sam; fi
   fi
done
```

## Summary of results
I want to reproduce a figure like the first one in `2024-10-03`, with current
mappings, to show the number of loci where at least *N* individuals have any
coverage.

```{bash}
if [ ! -e coverage_matrix.txt ]; then
   for i in $(cat samples.txt); do
      echo $i > z_$i.txt
      samtools view BAM/$i.bam | cut -f 3 | uniq | \
      gawk 'BEGIN{
         EXPECTED = 0
      }{
         CURRENT = substr($1, 4, 8) + 0
         for (i = EXPECTED; i < CURRENT; i++) {
            print 0
         }
         print 1
         EXPECTED = CURRENT + 1
      }END{
         for (i = EXPECTED; i <= 76849; i++) {
            print 0
         }
      }' >> z_$i.txt
   done
   echo "" > rownames.txt
   for i in $(seq 0 76849); do
      printf "loc%05i\n" $i >> rownames.txt
   done
   paste rownames.txt z_* > coverage_matrix.txt
   rm rownames.txt z_*
fi
```

```{r}
covMat <- read.table('coverage_matrix.txt')
PerLocus <- rowSums(covMat)
PerLocusTab <- as.data.frame(table(PerLocus), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
names(PerLocusTab) <- c('NumInd', 'NumLoci')
PerLocusTab$NumInd <- as.integer(PerLocusTab$NumInd)
PerLocusTab <- PerLocusTab[order(PerLocusTab$NumInd, decreasing = TRUE),]
PerLocusTab$CumSum <- cumsum(PerLocusTab$NumLoci)
plot(PerLocusTab$NumInd, PerLocusTab$CumSum,
     xlim = c(max(PerLocusTab$NumInd), min(PerLocusTab$NumInd)), type = 'l',
     xlab = 'Minimum number of individuals',
     ylab = 'Accumulated number of loci',
     main = 'Number of loci with at least so many individuals')
```

## Conclusions
Most loci are not covered yet in more than 60 individuals (out of 96), but therer
are more than 20000 loci covered at least by one read in more than 80 individuals,
and that's the low-coverage kind of data that ANGSD can help us with. Let's run it,
in a new folder.
